content: The Protein Nitrogen Unit (PNU) is a measurement used to quantify the amount of phosphotungstic acid-precipitable protein nitrogen, with 1 microgram (µg) being the standard unit. If you are interested in contributing to this topic, you are encouraged to apply to become the Editor-in-Chief. There can be one or multiple Editors-in-Chief for this subject. Alternatively, you may apply to serve as an Associate Editor-in-Chief for one of the subtopics listed under this area. To express your interest, please send an email indicating whether you wish to serve as the Editor-in-Chief for the entire topic or as an Associate Editor-in-Chief for a specific subtopic. Be sure to include your CV and/or a biographical sketch with your application. According to Russ Rowlett from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, the potency measurements of PNUs are highly dependent on the specific measurement techniques employed. Consequently, the results obtained from one manufacturer are not directly comparable to those from another. Due to this variability, while PNUs are still in use, they are gradually being replaced by Bioequivalent Allergy Units (BAUs). BAUs are determined through actual skin testing using reference preparations of standardized potency, providing a more reliable and consistent measure of allergen potency.
